newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly slide again on weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly slide again on weather.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices remained under pressure again Tuesday, with oversupply and forecasts for milder East Coast weather later this week and next still weighing on the market, industry sources said.
"There's a lot of storage and people don't know what to do with it," said one cash trader, noting soft demand this heating season has taken its toll on the complex.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent eased slightly to about $17.50 a barrel, with February one percent paper talked little changed at $17 despite softer crude, traders said.
NYH 2.2 percent slipped more than a quarter to $16.50-75, with high sulphur steady at near $16.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent slipped 25 cents to $16.00-25, with three percent more than 25 cents to $15 or under, traders said.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

Milder weather headed to New York this week continued to tank city gate gas prices, with swing off another 50 cents or more to the $3.50/mmBtu level. NYH one percent resid eased again to a $2.77/mmBtu equivalent.
